issues.legal_issue: Anticipatory bail may be refused when custodial interrogation is necessary to obtain material documents in a case involving serious allegations of forgery and false representations.
material_facts: The appeal challenged the refusal of anticipatory bail in a criminal investigation involving allegations that documents relating to property and a lease had been forged or altered.
The prosecution also alleged that false information and documents had been submitted to public authorities to obtain permission to run a school.
The Court considered that relevant documents were in the appellant’s possession and that custodial interrogation was necessary to obtain them and bring out the material information.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the refusal of anticipatory bail and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the mandate of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Court agreed that anticipatory bail was not warranted where custodial interrogation was necessary, particularly to secure documents alleged to have been forged or fabricated and to investigate representations allegedly made to a public authority. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: anticipatory_bail_appeal and serious_document_forgery_allegations and documents_in_applicant_possession and custodial_interrogation_needed_to_obtain_documents

predicates.anticipatory_bail_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the refusal of a request for protection from arrest.
predicates.serious_document_forgery_allegations: The prosecution alleges serious forgery or alteration of documents relevant to the investigation.
predicates.documents_in_applicant_possession: Relevant documents are said to be in the applicant’s possession.
predicates.custodial_interrogation_needed_to_obtain: The court considers custodial interrogation necessary to obtain relevant documents and investigative information.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges refusal of protection from arrest, serious document-forgery allegations are made, relevant documents are said to be with the applicant, and custodial interrogation is needed to obtain them, the outcome is refusal of anticipatory bail.

issues.legal_issue: Dismissal of an anticipatory bail appeal does not determine the merits of a later regular bail application.
material_facts: After dismissing the appeal, the Court vacated the interim protection and allowed the appellant time to surrender and seek regular bail.

The Court expressly stated that the decision concerned only eligibility for anticipatory bail and that the trial court remained free to decide a regular bail application independently and in accordance with law.
issues.conclusion: The trial court may decide a subsequent regular bail application independently, without being bound by the observations made on anticipatory bail.
issues.legal_principle: The Court limited its conclusion to eligibility for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and expressly preserved the trial court’s independent consideration of regular bail in accordance with law. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.anticipatory_bail_appeal_dismissed: The appellate court dismisses an appeal concerning refusal of protection from arrest.
predicates.applicant_permitted_to_seek_regular_bail: The applicant is allowed to surrender and seek regular bail before the trial court.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning protection from arrest is dismissed and the applicant is permitted to seek regular bail, the regular bail application is decided independently.
